newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says it has killed four Iraq-based rebels.
newsitem.headline: Iran says it has killed four Iraq-based rebels.

text.p: Iranian security forces killed four members of an Iraq-based opposition group on Saturday in western Iran, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported.

The agency quoted a security source in Ilam province as saying the security forces and local tribesmen clashed with six fighters of the opposition Mujahideen Khalq group who had crossed into Iran from Iraq. Two of the fighters escaped.
Last Sunday, five Mujahideen members were killed in a clash in another border area of the province, IRNA said.
In another incident in the past few weeks four Mujahideen members committed suicide by taking cyanide after being surrounded by security forces in the province.
It was apparently the first time this incident and last Sunday's clash had been reported.

The Mujahideen said on Friday an unspecified number of its members had been killed in clashes in the oil-rich Khuzestan province and in Ilam and Kermanshah provinces. The group said its forces had killed dozens of government troops.
Iran has not reported any casualties among its security forces.
Tehran said on Monday security forces and tribesmen killed five Mujahideen members and captured one in two separate clashes in Khuzestan and Kermanshah.

Iraq said on Wednesday three mortar bombs fired at the Mujahideen's Baghdad headquarters killed one person and injured several others. It blamed Iran for the attack. The Mujahideen also blamed Tehran and vowed to retaliate. Iran denied the charges.

Tehran has blamed the group, which has several camps in Iraq near the Iranian border, for cross-border attacks and bombings in the past few years. The Mujahideen has denied attacking civilians but has taken responsibility for striking at military and economic targets.
